one_liner: Header-only C++20 binary serializer using compile-time aggregate reflection; no schema, no codegen, faster than JSON via RapidJSON in third-party benchmarks.
what_it_does: zpp::bits serializes C++ structs/classes to and from a compact binary byte buffer, using compile-time reflection over aggregate (or structured-binding-compatible) members instead of an IDL or code generator. It also provides a lightweight RPC layer (client/server request dispatch by hashed function name) built on the same serialization core. The API is call-operator based (`out(obj1, obj2)` to serialize, `in(obj1, obj2)` to deserialize) and is not API- or wire-compatible with JSON libraries or Boost.Serialization.
how_it_is_fast: Member enumeration happens at compile time via structured bindings or an explicit `zpp::bits::members<N>` count, so there is no RTTI or runtime reflection, and the library is written almost entirely `constexpr` so the compiler can inline and specialize per type. It writes fields directly into a contiguous byte buffer (vector, array, or span) with no intermediate DOM/tree, unlike a JSON library that must build an object model. Field sizes can be fixed-width or opted out entirely, avoiding the text formatting and number parsing that JSON serialization pays for on every field.
when_to_use: Both ends of the wire are C++ and you control the schema, so a text/interop format isn't needed
Latency-sensitive object graphs (trading, telemetry) with primitives, vectors, optionals, or variants where nanosecond-scale serialize/deserialize matters
C++20 toolchain available (CI covers GCC 11-16 and Clang 13/17-22 on Linux and macOS) and types are aggregates or structured-binding-friendly
Want a single vendorable header (no build step, no schema compiler, no external dependency)
Need simple RPC (request/response dispatch) without standing up a separate schema/IDL toolchain
when_not_to_use: Need JSON or another human-readable/interoperable wire format — output is a custom binary layout, not JSON
Need cross-language interop without hand-porting the format — no schema/codegen like Protobuf, Cap'n Proto, or FlatBuffers provide
Targeting MSVC — CI does not cover it and users have hit internal compiler errors (issue #99) and VS2019 compile failures (issue #80)
Object graph contains std::vector<bool> — fails to compile as of the open issue #153 (std::_Bit_reference binding error)
Smallest possible message size matters more than speed — SimpleBinaryEncoding produced smaller messages in the same benchmark shootout

integration.dependencies: none (optionally detects and uses zpp::throwing if that header is present, for coroutine-based error handling)
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; CI tests GCC 11-16 and Clang 13, 17-22 on Ubuntu and macOS (Clang 17/18) — MSVC not in CI and has open compile-failure/ICE reports
integration.platforms: x86-64 and aarch64 (Linux and macOS in CI); no SIMD or architecture-specific intrinsics used
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different API and a custom binary wire format, not interchangeable with RapidJSON or other JSON libraries

gotchas: std::vector<bool> serialization does not compile (open issue #153)
Non-aggregate types need `using serialize = zpp::bits::members<N>;` (member count stated explicitly) or an ADL `serialize()` overload before C++26 lifts this requirement
RPC layer had a reported memory-leak bug (issue #188, closed) — confirm the fix is in the version you pin
Raw/non-owning pointers and null pointers are intentionally unsupported (README 'Limitations'); use std::optional instead
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick over Cap'n Proto when you don't want an IDL/schema-compiler step and want the fastest raw numbers in the same chronoxor/CppSerialization suite (34ns/37ns vs Cap'n Proto's 247ns/184ns); pick over the JSON-based siblings (cjson.cpp, DAW JSON Link, Tachyon.JSON, utl::json) whenever human-readable or cross-language JSON output isn't required and both ends are C++.
verified_claims_summary: In chronoxor/CppSerialization's trading-object-graph benchmark on Apple M1 Pro (macOS, CppBenchmark 'release' build, compiler/flags otherwise unstated), zpp::bits serialized in 34ns and deserialized in 37ns for a 130-byte message, versus RapidJSON-based JSON at 696ns/291ns for a 301-byte message — about 20x/7.9x faster. This compares a binary format to JSON text rather than the same facility, and the 291ns JSON-deserialize figure excludes a separately reported 771ns JSON-parse step.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-08-09; CI runs on push/PR and a daily cron against GCC 11-16 and Clang 13-22); MIT-licensed single 6,000-line header, trivially copyable/vendorable into a project with no package manager or build step.
